# Loading

```{r}
library("ape")
library("phangorn")
```

```{r}
data = read.nexus.data("simulations_data/simulated_traditions_22_07/sequences_0.nex")
names(data) = gsub("ms\\_|[|].*", "", names(data))
```

GT:
```{r}
# Need to define a standard trick to deal with internal nodes. Here, just added a subtree
gt = ape::read.tree(text="(((170[state=True:length=3],188[state=True:length=4])27[state=False:length=1],69[state=True:length=3])8[state=False:length=1],((93[state=True:length=0],((237[state=True:length=0])114[state=True:length=1]))74[state=False:length=2],226[state=True:length=2])25[state=False:length=2],296[state=True:length=7])0[state=False];")
plot(gt, "unrooted", main="GT Tree", show.node.label = TRUE)
```

# PCC

```{r}
library("stemmatology")

df = matrix(ncol = 8, data = as.numeric(unlist(data)))

res = PCC.Stemma(df, omissionsAsReadings = TRUE)
```



# Cladistics

```{r}
library("phangorn")
data = phyDat(data, type = "USER", levels = 0:10, ambiguity=NA)
```

## Neighbour-joining

Neighbour joining,
```{r}
dm <- dist.ml(data)
tree <- NJ(dm)
plot(tree, "unrooted", main="NJ unrooted tree")
Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
results[,1] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
```
```{r}
tree <- UNJ(dm)
plot(tree, "unrooted", main="UNJ unrooted tree")
results[,2] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, tree), similarity = TRUE)
```

## Maximum parsimony

```{r}
mm_start <- random.addition(data)
# Applying the pratchet method for maximum parsimony
# Default, fitch + SPR
mm_tree <- pratchet(data, start = mm_start, minit = 1000, maxit = 10000, all = TRUE, trace = 0, method = "fitch", rearrangements = "SPR", perturbation = "ratchet") # "The "fitch" algorithm only works correct for binary trees"
# Alternative
#mm_tree <- pratchet(data, start = mm_start, minit = 1000, maxit = 10000, all = TRUE, trace = 0, method = "sankoff", rearrangements = "SPR", perturbation = "ratchet")
```

```{r}
mm_tree
```

```{r}
parsimony(mm_tree, data)
```

```{r}
# Determining branch length
mm_tree <- acctran(mm_tree, data)
# Eliminating too short branches, to integrate polytomies/multifurcations
# we prune away internal edges of length tol (default = 1e-08), so our trees may contain multifurcations.
mm_tree  <- di2multi(mm_tree)
```

```{r}
# In case of several competing trees
#plot(consensus(mm_tree), "unrooted", main="Unrooted consensus tree")
#plotBS(mm_tree, type = "unrooted")
#plotBS(mm_tree)
plot(mm_tree, "unrooted", main="MP Unrooted tree")
results[,3] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, mm_tree), similarity = TRUE)
```

## Maximum likelihood

```{r}
# test different models
mt <- modelTest(data, model=c("JC", "F81", "K80", "HKY", "SYM", "GTR"), control = pml.control(trace = 0))
mt
```

```{r}
fit_mt <- pml_bb(mt, control = pml.control(trace = 0))
#fitGTR <- pml_bb(data, model="GTR")
```

And now bootstrapping,

```{r}
bs <- bootstrap.pml(fit_mt, bs=100, optNni=TRUE, control = pml.control(trace = 0))
```

```{r}
plotBS(midpoint(fit_mt$tree), p = .5, type="p", digits=2, main="Ultrafast bootstrap")
plotBS(midpoint(fit_mt$tree), bs, p = 50, type="p", main="Standard bootstrap")
#plotBS(midpoint(fit_mt$tree), bs, p = 50, type="p", digits=0, method = "TBE", main="Transfer bootstrap")
```
```{r}
results[,4] = Quartet::QuartetDivergence(Quartet::QuartetStatus(gt, fit_mt$tree), similarity = TRUE)
```


## Distance scoring

### Topology only
Quartet::QuartetStatus(tree1, tree2) or TreeDist::TripletDistance(tree1, tree2)

### With branch lengths

Kendall-Colijn (KC) Metric:What it does: Represents each rooted tree as a vector encoding the distance from the root to the Most Recent Common Ancestor (MRCA) of every pair of tips. A weight parameter $\lambda \in [0, 1]$ smoothly transitions the metric between pure topology ($\lambda = 0$) and topology weighted by branch length ($\lambda = 1$).Pros/Cons: Exceptional for rooted genealogies and phylodynamics.

R Implementation: treespace::treeDist(tree1, tree2, lambda = 0.5) or TreeDist::KendallColijn(tree1, tree2).

Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann (BHV) Geodesic Distance:What it does: Measures the shortest continuous path through continuous "tree space" accounting for topology shifts and edge lengths.
R Implementation: distory::dist.multiPhylo(c(tree1, tree2)).
